title: Review outcomes must reach every retained repair baseline
body: An initially clean repair baseline can later report the same advisory as new while another baseline owns it as original. Closing only the latter leaves automation incomplete. Apply assessments by stable finding identity to both original and new findings without deleting raw evidence. Share the current audit across baselines, but verify each original scope and history. Sequential hooks can reuse complete current audits; skipped checks must retry. Never reuse approval outcomes just because the current audit fingerprint matches: an assessment may cover an ignored path no longer mentioned in the current docs. The performance regression demonstrates that path appearing with an unchanged current-input fingerprint, and requires the original review to reopen. Keep raw check caching separate from review status, include review-record contents in publication fingerprints, and recheck original history and assessments on each invocation. Scope reviews to relevant document/manifest history so final metadata and unrelated commits preserve them. Explicit ignored-path presence needs its own observation because Git misses it. Decision findings consume existing authorized decision reviews, not a second approval path. Regressions cover multi-baseline closure, final commits, concurrent input changes and ignored review scopes; they do not establish semantic correctness or authenticated approval.

content.title: Review outcomes must reach every retained repair baseline
content.body: An initially clean repair baseline can later report the same advisory as a new finding while another retained baseline owns it as an original finding. Closing only the latter leaves automation permanently incomplete. Share assessments by stable finding identity and apply them to both original and new findings without deleting raw evidence. Keep raw check caching separate from review status, and include review-record contents in publication fingerprints so a concurrent assessment cannot publish stale closure. Bind review scope to relevant document/manifest history rather than HEAD alone: final metadata and unrelated commits must preserve it. Explicit ignored-path presence needs its own observation because Git alone misses it. Decision findings must consume the existing authorized decision history instead of creating a second approval path. These boundaries were exercised by the multi-baseline, final-commit, concurrency, and ignored-output regressions; they do not establish semantic correctness or authenticated approval.
